title: Derived semilinear sections and coefficient-linear geometric operations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be a strict inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings on it. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ consist of $B_n$-module sheaves $M_n$ and $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$, with compatible componentwise morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Equivalently these are modules over the ring object $B_\bullet$ in the topos of inverse sequences of sheaves on $\mathcal C$. This is a Grothendieck abelian category with componentwise exactness. Use ordinary unbounded cochain complexes and derived categories [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Evaluation induces exact functors $e_n:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(B_n)$, computed termwise, jointly detecting isomorphisms. For $m\geq n$, the transitions induce natural reduction maps $t_{m,n}:M_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n\to M_n$, compatible with composition through the canonical tensor associators [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. An object is called normalized, or cartesian, when all these maps are isomorphisms. No flatness of the coefficient maps is assumed.

Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi presented by small sites, an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits, and put $C_n=u^{-1}B_n$. Exact levelwise inverse image gives $V=u^{-1}_\bullet:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(\mathscr S(C))$. Levelwise module direct image has a total right derived functor $G=Ru_{*,\bullet}$ and $V\dashv G$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms $e_nV=u^{-1}e_n$ and $e_nG\cong Ru_{*,n}e_n$, compatible with the units, counits and transition maps. In extension form the transitions of $GN$ are $G_n(t^N_{m,n})\circ b_{m,n,N_m}$, where $G_n=Ru_{*,n}$, $T_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$, $S_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{C_m}C_n$, and $b_{m,n}:T_{m,n}G_m\to G_nS_{m,n}$ is the mate of the inverse of $S_{m,n}u^{-1}\cong u^{-1}T_{m,n}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For an open localization, exact extension by zero $j_!$ and restriction act on systems and their derived categories, with the ordinary level adjunctions [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].

For a compatible map $B_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ of ring systems, derived extension of scalars is defined on these ordinary derived categories and evaluates to $M_n\otimes^L_{B_n}D_n$. Derived tensor of systems evaluates to $M_n\otimes^L_{B_n}N_n$. These operations use K-flat resolutions and the total tensor complex [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $H_B(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{B_\bullet}(M,N)$ be internal Hom on the ringed topos of systems [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For cartesian $M$ and arbitrary $N$, there are canonical natural identifications $e_nH_B(M,N)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_n}(M_n,N_n)$, carrying system evaluation to ordinary tensor-Hom evaluation. Its reduction transition is the transpose of
$$S(H_m)\otimes^L M_n\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_{m,n}^{M,-1}}S(H_m)\otimes^L S(M_m)\cong S(H_m\otimes^L M_m)\xrightarrow{S(\mathrm{ev})}S(N_m)\xrightarrow{t^N_{m,n}}N_n,$$
where in this formula $S=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$ and $H_m=R\mathcal Hom_{B_m}(M_m,N_m)$. No fiberwise-Hom formula is asserted for noncartesian first inputs.

Pullback-composition identifications, maps of module sheaves, the preceding tensor and evaluation maps, and units and counits give natural transformations on the ordinary derived categories of systems. Their specified exchange maps are the ordinary adjunction-mate words; this includes open-adjunction exchange and composites with proper direct-image composition. The coefficient projection comparison for $Ru_*$ is precisely $b_{m,n}$ above. The general tensor projection map is the transpose of $u^{-1}(Ru_*N\otimes^LP)\cong u^{-1}Ru_*N\otimes^Lu^{-1}P\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_N\otimes1}N\otimes^Lu^{-1}P$. Evaluation, composition and taking these specified adjunction transposes agree with the levelwise constructions and ordinary mate-pasting identities. These assertions concern maps actually constructed on $D(\mathscr S(B))$, without a claim that evaluations detect equality of arbitrary morphisms, that comparisons are invertible on arbitrary inputs, or that evaluated K-injective systems are K-injective. No right adjoint on the subcategory of normalized systems is asserted.

proof.text: Obtain the ordinary system calculus and its Hom reduction formula from [lem-coef-semilinear-system-existence]. Obtain geometric pullback/direct image with PullTransitionFormula, coefficient extension, and open localization from [lem-coef-semilinear-operations-existence]. These are two separate construction parts of the original statement.

For a geometric operation, reduction naturality follows by applying the injective scalar adjunction transpose and naturality of derivedTransition. Apply that naturality to the derived geometric counit. Substitute PullTransitionFormula and counitEvaluation. The defining mateEquiv counit identity for coefficientMate and cancellation of the evaluated pullback isomorphisms give TransitionFormula. This is push_transition_of_pull in Lean; no joint faithfulness on derived morphisms is used.

Prove evaluation_transpose by substituting the two adjunction homEquiv-unit formulas, unitEvaluation, naturality of pullEvaluation and pushEvaluation, and the inverse isomorphism identities. Apply this formula to tensorProjection, which is the transpose of tensorPullback followed by counit tensor identity. Expand tensorPullback_evaluation and counitEvaluation and use naturality of levelTensorPullback. This gives ProjectionEvaluation. Assemble the original SemilinearDerivedSectionsData without changing its fields or quantifiers. The already proved evaluation_mate remains unchanged.
